questions.prompt: Sort each substance: element, compound or mixture?
questions.hint: Element = one kind of atom. Compound = different atoms chemically joined. Mixture = not joined.
questions.explain: Elements: iron, oxygen, gold. Compounds: water, carbon dioxide, salt. Mixtures: air, salt water, brass.

options: A substance made of only one kind of atom
Two substances mixed together
Any substance that is a solid
A substance made of molecules
questions.explain: An element contains only one kind of atom and can't be broken down into simpler substances chemically.

questions.prompt: Oxygen gas is made of O₂ molecules. Is it an element or a compound?
options: Compound, because it's made of molecules
Element, because both atoms are oxygen
Mixture
Neither

feedback.0: A molecule is only a compound if it contains DIFFERENT kinds of atoms.

questions.explain: Both atoms in O₂ are oxygen, so oxygen gas is an element made of molecules.

questions.prompt: Match each element to its symbol.
questions.explain: Some symbols come from Latin names: Fe (ferrum), Au (aurum), Na (natrium).

questions.prompt: A grey-yellow powder is tested with a magnet. Grey bits jump onto the magnet. What is the powder?
options: The compound iron sulfide
A mixture of iron and sulfur
Pure sulfur
Pure iron
questions.explain: In a mixture, iron keeps its magnetic property. In the compound iron sulfide, it doesn't.

questions.prompt: Which are true for a COMPOUND? Choose all that apply.
options: Elements are chemically joined
Elements are in a fixed ratio
It has properties different from its elements
It can be separated with a magnet or filter
Energy is usually given out or taken in when it forms
questions.explain: Compounds need chemical reactions to be separated, not physical methods like magnets or filters.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentences about water, H₂O.
questions.text: Water is a ___ . Each molecule has ___ hydrogen atoms joined to ___ oxygen atom.
questions.explain: H₂O: the small 2 means two hydrogen atoms; no number after O means one oxygen atom.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are in ONE molecule of carbon dioxide, CO₂?
questions.hint: Count the C, then look at the small number after O.

questions.prompt: Sodium explodes in water and chlorine is a poisonous gas, but salt (NaCl) is safe to eat. This shows that…
options: salt is a mixture of sodium and chlorine
a compound has different properties from its elements
sodium and chlorine are both safe
salt contains no sodium
questions.explain: When elements chemically combine, the compound has brand-new properties.

questions.prompt: Put the Iron + Sulfur investigation in a sensible order.
steps: Observe the properties of iron and sulfur separately
Mix them and test the mixture with a magnet
Heat the mixture strongly (teacher, fume cupboard)
Test the new black solid with a magnet
Compare the results and draw a conclusion
questions.explain: Observe → mix and test → react → test the product → conclude.

questions.prompt: Give THREE differences between a mixture and a compound.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) In a mixture substances are not chemically joined; in a compound elements are chemically joined. 2) A mixture's parts can be in any ratio; a compound has a fixed ratio. 3) A mixture keeps the properties of its parts and can be separated by physical methods; a compound has new properties and needs a chemical reaction to separate.
rubric: New properties vs keeps properties, OR chemical vs physical separation
questions.explain: These are the key differences examiners look for.
